definitions.gloss: attention seeker; show-off; person who loves the spotlight
definitions.explanation: A person who constantly wants to stand out and be noticed. Formed from the verb 目立つ (to stand out) + たがる (to want to) + 屋 (person characterized by a trait).

examples.japanese: あの{子|こ}は{目立|めだ}ちたがり{屋|や}だ。
examples.english: That kid is an attention seeker.

examples.japanese: {目立|めだ}ちたがり{屋|や}の{彼女|かのじょ}はいつも{派手|はで}な{服|ふく}を{着|き}ている。
examples.english: She's an attention seeker and always wears flashy clothes.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}は{目立|めだ}ちたがり{屋|や}だったが、{大人|おとな}になって{落|お}ち{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: I was an attention seeker as a child, but I calmed down as an adult.

notes:
A compound word built from three parts: {目立|めだ}つ (to stand out) + たがる (to want to, to be eager to) + {屋|や} (person characterized by a trait). The suffix {屋|や} in this sense describes someone who habitually does something, often with a mildly critical or affectionate tone.

FORMATION PATTERN:
The ~たがり{屋|や} pattern creates words for people who want to do something:
- {目立|めだ}ちたがり{屋|や}: wants to stand out
- {寂|さび}しがり{屋|や}: easily lonely
- {怖|こわ}がり{屋|や}: easily scared
- {恥|は}ずかしがり{屋|や}: easily embarrassed, shy

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目立|めだ}ちたがり{屋|や}の{性格|せいかく}: an attention-seeking personality
- {目立|めだ}ちたがり{屋|や}な{人|ひと}: an attention-seeking person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見栄|みえ}っ{張|ぱ}り: show-off — focused on appearing superior or wealthier
- {自己顕示欲|じこけんじよく}が{強|つよ}い: having a strong desire for self-display — more formal
- {出|で}たがり: someone who wants to appear (on TV, in public) — similar but focused on appearing in media
